name: GitHub
description: GitHub is a software development platform for hosting Git repositories and collaborating through issues and pull requests. Teams use it to plan work, review changes, discuss code, and maintain shared software projects.
agentUseSummary: Connect GitHub once, then choose which agents may search repositories, read issues and pull requests, prepare comments, or post comments under Safe or Dangerous policy.

capabilities.label: Find repositories
capabilities.description: Search up to twenty-five repositories visible to the authorized GitHub user.

capabilities.label: Read issues
capabilities.description: List up to fifty issues from one explicit repository.

capabilities.label: Read pull requests
capabilities.description: List up to fifty pull requests from one explicit repository.

capabilities.label: Prepare comments
capabilities.description: Prepare one bounded issue or pull-request comment locally without changing GitHub.

capabilities.label: Comment on issues
capabilities.description: Post one exact comment to an explicit issue.

capabilities.label: Comment on pull requests
capabilities.description: Post one exact conversation comment to an explicit pull request.

allowed.label: Search repositories
allowed.description: Search a bounded set of repositories visible to the authorized GitHub user.

allowed.label: List issues
allowed.description: List a bounded set of issues in one explicit repository.

allowed.label: List pull requests
allowed.description: List a bounded set of pull requests in one explicit repository.

allowed.label: Prepare a comment
allowed.description: Prepare one issue or pull-request comment locally without changing GitHub.

approvalRequired.label: Comment on an issue
approvalRequired.description: Post one exact comment to an explicit issue; Safe mode requires matching approval.

approvalRequired.label: Comment on a pull request
approvalRequired.description: Post one exact conversation comment to an explicit pull request; Safe mode requires matching approval.

blocked.label: Delete repositories
blocked.description: Repository deletion is outside the bounded V1 connector.

blocked.label: Change governance or security
blocked.description: Organization administration, branch protections, rulesets, secrets, and security-control changes are outside V1.

blocked.label: Use arbitrary GitHub API calls
blocked.description: Raw URLs, arbitrary operations, tokens, and unbounded pagination are never exposed to agents.

blocked.label: Rewrite protected history
blocked.description: Force pushes and protected-history rewrites are outside V1.

approvalProfiles.label: Safe
approvalProfiles.description: Repository searches, bounded reads, and local drafts run directly; each posted comment requires matching approval.

approvalProfiles.label: Dangerously skip permissions
approvalProfiles.description: Every selected GitHub operation supported by this connector runs without Relay per-action approval; connection ownership, GitHub App permissions, user authority, repository selection, request bounds, audits, redaction, and GitHub limits still apply.

runtimeSupport.description: Railway mounts six typed GitHub tools and attaches the connected GitHub user token server-side without exposing it to the agent.
Railway mounts six typed GitHub tools and attaches the connected GitHub user token server-side without exposing it to the agent.

providerSetup.blocker: Relay Console's public GitHub App, production callback and setup URL, requested repository permissions, app slug, client credentials, and a fresh production authorization have not been configured and verified.
providerSetup.nextAction: Create or configure Relay Console as a public GitHub App, allow installation by any account, leave Request user authorization during installation off, register https://api.relayconsole.work/api/v1/marketplace/oauth/github/callback as both the callback URL and setup URL, grant metadata read plus issues read/write and pull-request read permissions, configure GITHUB_APP_SLUG, GITHUB_CLIENT_ID, and GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET on Railway, then verify installation binding, PKCE, state, user binding, repository search, bounded reads, Safe comment approval, Dangerous comment posting, refresh, revocation, disconnect, and post-disconnect denial.

evidence.supports: GitHub documents public GitHub App registration, callback and setup URLs, installation authorization, requested permissions, user authorization during installation, and app distribution settings.

GitHub documents the user access-token authorization-code flow, state, PKCE S256, exact callback handling, token exchange, refresh tokens, and the intersection of user authority with GitHub App permissions.
GitHub documents direct public installation URLs with a state parameter, which Relay uses to bind the selected installation to the OAuth transaction.
GitHub documents the post-installation setup redirect and installation_id parameter and requires the receiving app to verify that installation instead of trusting the callback value alone.
GitHub documents revoking one GitHub App user token with the app client ID and client secret; Relay calls this endpoint before clearing a disconnected connection.
GitHub documents authenticated repository search and bounded per-page results; Relay follows only one page and caps output at twenty-five repositories.
GitHub documents repository issue listing and notes that the Issues endpoint also returns pull requests; Relay filters pull-request records and caps output at fifty issues.
GitHub documents repository pull-request listing with explicit owner, repository, state, and pagination parameters; Relay follows only one bounded page.
GitHub documents one issue-comment endpoint for both issues and pull-request conversations and the required Issues write permission; Relay wraps one exact bounded comment.
